summary_paragraph: The patient, a woman with chronic pancreatitis, depression, anxiety, and a history of venous thrombosis and C. difficile, was readmitted with abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting consistent with an acute flare of her chronic pancreatitis. She had difficulty with IV access, requiring a midline catheter placement after failed PICC attempts. She was managed with IV fluids, analgesics, and antiemetics, then transitioned to oral tramadol and a regular diet as her symptoms improved. Her lipase was normal, and stool testing ruled out C. difficile. Hypertension was managed with lisinopril and the addition of amlodipine. She remained mentally stable, tolerated discharge on a regular diet, and was sent home with all home medications and follow-up instructions.
problems: Major depressive affective disorder, single episode, unspecified
Personal history of venous thrombosis and embolism
